![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248996/assets/812e1c08b671e54023a65dc5b9fbf089ddd27781ad555d6fb9e4d2a9816d193f.png)

Consider the triangle $△ABC$ shown above. The line segment $\overset{―}{AH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overset{―}{BC}.$ If $m∠ACB={125}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠HAC.$
q-27826.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠ACB & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{125}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA & ={55}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $△AHC$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC & ={180}^{∘} \\ {55}^{∘}+m∠HAC+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC+{145}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC & ={35}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Consider the triangle △ABC shown above. The line segment AH― is the altitude corresponding to BC―. If m∠ACB=125∘, calculate m∠HAC.

a
40∘
b
35∘
c
30∘
d
37∘
e
45∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the straight angle must have a measure of 180∘, we have m∠HCA+m∠ACB=180∘m∠HCA+125∘=180∘m∠HCA=55∘.

Note that △AHC is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to 180∘, we have m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC=180∘55∘+m∠HAC+90∘=180∘m∠HAC+145∘=180∘m∠HAC=35∘.

Given $△PQR$ shown above, which of the following diagrams represents the height corresponding to $\overset{―}{PR}?$
q-118702.worked_solution:
The height (or altitude) corresponding to $\overset{―}{PR}$ is a line segment that 

- runs from the opposite vertex $Q$ to the line $\overset{⟷}{PR},$ and

- is perpendicular to $\overset{⟷}{PR}.$

To draw the height, we proceed as follows:

- Extend the line segment $\overset{―}{PR}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248996/assets/664c9507be2e02908b8a151d0c58222545a84a7d71648c28e61badfb23e1981b.png)

- Draw the perpendicular from $Q$ to $\overset{⟷}{PR}.$
